All samples were analyzed on UltiMate 3000 RSLCnano system (Dionex – Thermo Scientific) coupled to a TripleTOF 5600 mass spectrometer with a NanoSpray III source (Sciex). The instrument was operated with Analyst TF 1.7 (Sciex). The peptides were trapped and desalted with 2 % acetonitrile in 0.1 % formic acid at flow rate of 5 μL/min on Acclaim PepMap100 column (5 μm, 2 cm×100 μm ID, Thermo Scientific). Eluted peptides were separated using Acclaim PepMap100 analytical column (3 μm, 25 cm×75 μm ID, Thermo Scientific). The 70 min elution gradient at constant flow of 300 nl/min was set to 5 % of phase B (0.1 % formic acid in 99.9 % acetonitrile, phase A 0.1 % formic acid) for first 5 min, then with gradient elution by increasing content of acetonitrile. TOF MS mass range was set to 350–1500 m/z, in MS/MS mode the instrument acquired fragmentation spectra within m/z range 100-2000.

steps.title: Quantify cccDNA levels by qPCR
steps.instruction: Analyze cccDNA levels using an Eppendorf realplex Master cycler and gb Elite PCR Master Mix (Generi Biotech).

substeps.instruction: Prepare a reaction mix containing 5 µl of T5 exonuclease-treated DNA, 0.6 µl of cccDNA-F primer 5′- CCGTGTGCACTTCGCTTCA -3′ (10 µM), 0.6 µl of cccDNA-R primer 5′- GCACAGCTTGGAGGCTTGA -3′ (10 µM), 0.4 µl of cccDNA probe 5′-[FAM]CATGGAGACCACCGTGAACGCCC[BHQ1]-3′ (5 µM), 10 µl of 2x gb Elite Master Mix, and 3.4 µl of PCR grade water.

Run qPCR with the following thermal cycling conditions: denaturation (95°C for 10 min), followed by 40 cycles of denaturation (95°C for 15 s) and annealing/elongation (60°C for 1 min) with fluorescence measurement at the end of the elongation step.

steps.title: Normalize cccDNA levels to albumin
steps.instruction: Normalize cccDNA levels by determining albumin levels via qPCR using the same thermal cycling conditions as the cccDNA amplification.

substeps.instruction: Use primers Alb-F 5'-GCTGTCATCTCTTGTGGGCTGT-3', Alb-R 5'-AAACTCATGGGAGCTGCTGGTT-3', and Alb-probe 5'-[FAM]GGAGAGATTTGTGTGGGCATGACAGG[BHQ1]-3'.

steps.title: Perform Co-Immunoprecipitation (Co-IP)
steps.instruction: Isolate protein complexes using a cold co-immunoprecipitation buffer.

substeps.instruction: Wash transfected cells with pre-chilled 1xPBS.
Add cold co-immunoprecipitation buffer (20 mM HEPES [pH 7.9], 50 mM NaCl, 5 mM EDTA, 1% (v/v) Igepal CA-630, 10% (v/v) glycerol, 1 mM dithiothreitol).
Scrape cells and transfer into 1.5 ml Eppendorf tubes.
Incubate on ice with frequent mixing for 20 min.
Centrifuge at 14,000 g, 4 °C, for 20 min and transfer the supernatant to fresh tubes.
Estimate protein concentration using Coomassie (Bradford) Protein Assay Kit (Pierce).

steps.title: Prepare anti-HA Magnetic Beads for Co-IP
steps.instruction: Prepare and wash magnetic beads for the capture of HA-tagged proteins.

substeps.instruction: Pipet 25 µl of magnetic beads (Pierce) into a 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube for each sample.
Wash beads three times: wash with 1 ml of 1x PBS, gently vortex to mix, and remove supernatant using a magnetic stand.

steps.title: Capture HA-tagged proteins
steps.instruction: Incubate the protein sample with prepared magnetic beads.

substeps.instruction: Add the sample containing HA-tagged protein (400 µg of total protein diluted in 600 µl of lysis buffer) to the pre-washed magnetic beads.
Incubate at 4 °C for 4 h to overnight with constant mixing.
Collect beads with a magnetic stand, remove the unbound sample, and save it for analysis.
Wash beads five times with 1 ml of lysis buffer.

steps.title: Analyze Co-IP results
steps.instruction: Denature and analyze the precipitated proteins.

substeps.instruction: Denature bound proteins in 2x sample loading buffer by boiling at 100 °C for 5 min.
Analyze proteins by SDS-PAGE and Western blot.

steps.title: Prepare cell lysates for IP
steps.instruction: Extract proteins from transfected cells two days post-transfection.

substeps.instruction: Wash cells with ice-cold 1xPBS.

Scrape cells into lysis buffer (2% SDS, 150 mM NaCl, 10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.0, supplemented with 2mM sodium orthovanadate, 50 mM sodium fluoride, 10 mM N-ethylmaleimide (NEM) and protease inhibitors) into 1.5 ml Eppendorf tubes, using approximately 500 µl lysis buffer per T75 flask.
Denature samples by boiling at 100°C for 10 min.
Dilute lysates with 9 volumes of dilution buffer (10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.0, 150 mM NaCl, 2 mM EDTA, 1% Triton).
Centrifuge lysates at maximum speed for 20 min in a table-top Eppendorf centrifuge and transfer the supernatant to a fresh tube.
Estimate protein concentration using Coomassie (Bradford) Protein Assay Kit (Pierce).

steps.title: Perform Immunoprecipitation (IP) of cell lysates
steps.instruction: Capture proteins from the prepared cell lysates using magnetic beads.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 25 µl of magnetic beads per sample by washing three times with 1 ml of 1x PBS (vortex and remove supernatant via magnetic stand).
Pipet 25 µl of washed magnetic beads into 500 µg of cell lysate (up to 1500 µg may be used if protein expression is very low).
Incubate the mixture with constant rotating at 4°C overnight.
Collect beads using a magnetic stand, remove the unbound sample, and save for analysis.
Wash beads three times with 1 ml of wash buffer (10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.0, 1 M NaCl, 1 mM EDTA, 1% NP-40).

steps.title: Analyze IP results for Ubiquitination
steps.instruction: Denature and analyze the precipitated proteins for ubiquitin.

substeps.instruction: Denature bound proteins in 2x sample loading buffer by boiling at 100 °C for 5 min.
Analyze proteins by SDS-PAGE and Western blot with anti-Ubiquitin antibodies (Cell Signaling).

steps.title: Process SDS-PAGE gel for Mass Spectrometry
steps.instruction: Digest proteins from a Coomassie-stained gel for peptide analysis.

substeps.instruction: Divide the Coomassie-stained gel into 14 pieces.
Destain gel pieces with ammonium bicarbonate in 50% acetonitrile at 30°C for 30 min.
Dry pieces with 200 µl acetonitrile for 5 min at 30°C.
Reduce cysteins with dithiothreitol (65°C, 30 min) and alkylate with Iodoacetamide (RT for 30 min in dark).
Digest proteins with 0.1 µg of trypsin solution in ammonium bicarbonate at 37°C for 10 hours.
Extract peptides with 50 µl of 2% TFA and 50 µl of 60% acetonitrile.
Dry peptides in a SpeedVac and dissolve in 15 µl of 0.1% formic acid.

steps.title: Process IP proteins on beads for Mass Spectrometry
steps.instruction: Digest proteins directly from magnetic beads for peptide analysis.

substeps.instruction: Wash immunoprecipitated proteins on magnetic beads 3x with 1ml of 50 mM ammonium hydrocarbonate.
Reduce proteins with dithiothreitol (65°C, 30 min) and alkylate with Iodoacetamide (RT for 30 min in dark).
Remove solvent and add 100ul of 50 mM ammonium hydrocarbonate containing 0.1 µg of chymotrypsin.
Digest proteins at 37°C for 10 hours.
Separate peptides from beads by magnet, dry in a SpeedVac (Labconco), and dissolve in 15 µl of 0.1% formic acid.
